claimChanges.claimText: CUHK leaves pedagogical AI rules to course teacher discretion. For example, Chung Chi College General Education courses (GECC3130/4130, AY2026/27) adopt Approach 2 ('Use only with prior permission'), where GenAI is prohibited for drafting written assignments but permitted for spelling and grammar checking, subject to approval by the Senate Committee on General Education (university-wide full student guide rules remain unverified behind ADFS SSO).

At CUHK, improper or unauthorized use of AI tools in learning activities and assessments constitutes academic dishonesty (including plagiarism or unauthorized third-party assistance) under Senate policy (effective from AY2025-26, updated July 2026), subject to penalties ranging from zero marks to demerits, suspension, or termination of studies, adjudicated by the course-offering faculty/college or the Faculty of Medicine Fitness to Practice (FTP) Committee.

Penalties for academic dishonesty involving AI tools at CUHK may include zero marks on the assessment, marking down of overall course grade, a demerit recorded on academic transcript, or course failure (e.g. assignments with VeriGuide AWD AI Index > 25% under Approach 2 in GECC3130/4130 may receive a failing grade), and for severe offences, suspension or termination of studies under Senate procedures (effective from AY2025-26, updated July 2026).

In General Education course GECC4130 (AY2026/27), students must submit a signed academic honesty declaration with each assignment confirming awareness of university regulations, and acknowledging that submissions may be investigated by AI content detection software (VeriGuide AWD). A university-wide declaration or prompt-logging rule has not been established in public evidence because the Student Guide to Academic Honesty remains restricted behind ADFS SSO; students follow individual course instructions.

CUHK's Enterprise AI Hub instructs users to verify important facts, sources, citations, calculations and generated outputs, and to follow course-level instructions on permitted use and acknowledgement.

CUHK's Enterprise AI Hub instructs users not to enter personal data, confidential information, restricted research data or other protected University information unless the specific service and use case have been approved for that data.

Microsoft Copilot Chat (Basic) is available to all CUHK students and staff at no charge under the University's current Microsoft 365 licences. CUHK ITSC guidance says that after CUHK login, chat data is protected and would not be stored by Microsoft; users sign in with their CUHK email and DUO authentication and should check the enterprise data protection indicator.

CUHK provides Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) with integration into Microsoft 365 applications and institutional context.
